messages:
alex.k: quick question — for the new internal control-plane API, should we commit to a single typed HTTP/JSON surface or standardize on gRPC + protos? thinking about telemetry correlation and quota propagation across edge -> runtime :thinking:

maya: my vote: typed JSON HTTP. easier for browser/UIs and quick SDKs. avoids need for gRPC-web hacks.

sam: +1 for gRPC/proto for internal services. strong typing, smaller wire payloads, streaming for KV cache priming. also improves interoperability for internal infra. :thumbsup:

rina: worried about the client side though — product teams call the control plane from lambda + browser + infra agents. gRPC in browser is rough unless we proxy. how do we preserve per-request routing metadata (tenant, route-priority) if we transcode at the edge?

alex.k: exactly. main tradeoffs: ease-of-use for product/front-end vs operational guarantees (typed contracts, streaming). also telemetry: we want a single correlation id that survives proxy transcoding and fallbacks.

sam: we could require a minimal set of headers that must be passed through the gateway unchanged: `x-rd-corr`, `x-rd-tenant`, `x-rd-routing`. gateways already set those when absent. keep them immutable.

maya: that's fine but we still need client ergonomics. proposal: public-facing HTTP JSON surface + backend-only gRPC between infra components. gateway does strict header passthrough and verifies `x-rd-tenant` mapping. SDKs do JSON for devs but compile to gRPC for internal services.

rina: can we avoid heavy runtime proxies? I'd rather a small shim sidecar per service that speaks gRPC internally and exposes a tiny HTTP JSON shim for legacy callers. sidecar handles quota tokens and injects `x-rd-corr`. lightweight and incremental.

alex.k: rollout plan idea: phase 1 - HTTP JSON shim + SDK changes (low risk). phase 2 - enable gRPC between sidecars for high-throughput routes. phase 3 - flip internal-only services to proto-first and deprecate public shim. that gives us canary windows for telemetry regressions.

sam: sounds pragmatic. we should also add automated checks in the console: a telemetry drift alert if correlation ids drop >5% during canary. link metric name: `infra.correlation.missing_rate`.

maya: +1. and quota UX: make quota diagnostic in console show header-level lineage. show the last hop that stamped the token. otherwise support will be triaging blind.

rina: small example of shim header enforcement we can ship:
```
# pseudo-config
required_headers: ["x-rd-corr","x-rd-tenant","x-rd-routing"]
on_missing: set_and_log
on_change: reject
```

alex.k: love it. last bit — optelemetry: ensure spans include `routing.policy` tag and `quota.bucket`. that will let us correlate cost/latency regressions to routing changes.

ops-bot: deploy-check: inferred impact on 3 services (control-plane, routing-proxy, sdk-service). suggested canary group: 2% traffic, 4h window.

maya: OK let's draft an RFC with phases + telemetry SLO checks. I'll start and post a draft.

sam: ping me on the RFC for proto defs and streaming contract. happy to sketch flow.

rina: I'll add a sidecar PoC and a tiny e2e test that asserts header passthrough.

alex.k: thanks all — keeping this pragmatic and incremental will save support tickets. :white_check_mark:
